reason: Section 14.1 contains separate study topics: claims with no limitation period, retrospective revival, and limits for settled or finally dismissed claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No limitation period for specified assault and battery claims
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 14.1(1) states when there is no limitation period for trespass to the person, assault, or battery claims.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the sexual-nature, intimate-relationship, and dependency conditions that remove the limitation period for these claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Retrospective application and revived dismissed claims
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14.1(2) and 14.1(3) address claims before or after commencement and proceedings previously dismissed solely because a limitation period expired.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 14.1 applies despite prior expiry and how it revives certain dismissed claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Settled and finally dismissed claims excluded
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 14.1(4) identifies settled claims and finally dismissed claims to which the section does not apply.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which settled or finally dismissed claims remain outside section 14.1.

reason: Section 15 has two distinct deemed-knowledge rules, one for agents of principals and one for successors in property-related claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Agent knowledge attributed to principal
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 15(1) deems a principal to know specified matters based on an agent with actual knowledge and a communication duty.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an agent's actual knowledge is deemed to be the principal's knowledge.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Predecessor knowledge attributed to successor claimant
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 15(2) deems a successor claimant to know specified matters based on a predecessor or the claimant.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a predecessor's knowledge affects a successor claimant.

reason: Section 16 sets out two different consequences when a defendant wilfully conceals the existence of a claim.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Concealment blocks reliance on expiry as a defence

evidenceText: the defendant cannot rely on the expiry of a limitation period

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraph 16(a) prevents a defendant who wilfully concealed a claim from relying on listed expired limitation periods as a defence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when wilful concealment prevents a defendant from relying on an expired limitation period.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Later deadline for specified concealed claims

evidenceText: the claim shall not be brought after the later of

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraph 16(b) states the later deadline for specified claims when wilful concealment has occurred.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the later-of test for specified claims after wilful concealment.

reason: The target contains one operative rule suspending limitation periods while the claimant is a minor.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Suspension of limitation periods while claimant is a minor
proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one operative rule suspending limitation periods while the claimant is a minor.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that limitation periods established by the Act are suspended while the claimant is a minor.

reason: Section 18 pairs the suspension of listed limitation periods during incapacity with an extension rule when less than one year remains.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Incapacity suspension and one-year extension
proposedGroups.reason: Section 18 pairs the suspension of listed limitation periods during incapacity with an extension rule when less than one year remains.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how incapacity suspends listed limitation periods and how the one-year extension operates when suspension ends.

reason: Section 19 separates the effect of an acknowledgment, the required form and recipients, and exclusions for without-prejudice or reserved-rights correspondence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Acknowledgment restarts the limitation period
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(1) states that a timely acknowledgment begins the limitation period again.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an acknowledgment restarts the operation of a limitation period.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Writing and recipient requirements for acknowledgment
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(2) sets writing, maker, and recipient requirements for an acknowledgment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must make an acknowledgment, who may receive it, and that it must be in writing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Correspondence that is not an acknowledgment
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(3) excludes without-prejudice admissions and statements reserving the limitation defence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which settlement correspondence is not an acknowledgment.

reason: Section 20 separates the part-payment restart rule, who must make and receive the payment, and payments that do not restart time.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Part payment restarts the limitation period
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 20(1) states that a timely part payment of a monetary obligation begins the limitation period again.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a part payment restarts the operation of a limitation period.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required payer and recipient for part payment
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 20(2) identifies who must make and receive the part payment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must make a part payment and who may receive it.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Payments excluded from the restart rule
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 20(3) excludes full payment, without-prejudice payment, non-acceptance of further liability, and reserved limitation defences.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which payments do not restart the limitation period.

reason: Section 21 contains separate conditions for adding claims after expiry depending on whether the change is between existing parties, defendants, or claimants.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Added claims between existing parties

evidenceText: does not change the capacity in which either party sues or is sued

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraph 21(a) permits an added related claim between parties without changing their litigation capacity.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the condition for adding a related claim between existing parties after expiry.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Added or substituted defendant after expiry

evidenceText: adds or substitutes a defendant or changes the capacity in which a defendant is sued

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraph 21(b) permits adding or substituting a defendant if timely knowledge prevents merits prejudice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the knowledge and prejudice condition for adding or substituting a defendant.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Added or substituted claimant after expiry

evidenceText: adds or substitutes a claimant or changes the capacity in which a claimant sues

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraph 21(c) adds an effective-determination or enforcement requirement for claimant changes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the knowledge, prejudice, and necessity conditions for adding or substituting a claimant.

reason: Section 22 states when defendant actions or assurances that caused reasonable delay allow a claim within six months after the belief is known to be unfounded.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Six-month period after defendant-caused delay
proposedGroups.reason: Section 22 states when defendant actions or assurances that caused reasonable delay allow a claim within six months after the belief is known to be unfounded.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conditions that allow a delayed claimant to bring a claim within six months after learning settlement belief was unfounded.

reason: Section 23 defines non-judicial remedy and bars enforcement of that remedy when a limitation period prevents bringing the claim.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Non-judicial remedy definition and expiry effect
proposedGroups.reason: Section 23 defines non-judicial remedy and bars enforcement of that remedy when a limitation period prevents bringing the claim.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what counts as a non-judicial remedy and how expiry of the limitation period affects enforcement.

reason: Section 24 states when the Act applies to New Brunswick claims governed by another jurisdiction's substantive law and when another jurisdiction's limitations law bars the claim.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Conflict of laws limitation rules
proposedGroups.reason: Section 24 states when the Act applies to New Brunswick claims governed by another jurisdiction's substantive law and when another jurisdiction's limitations law bars the claim.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how New Brunswick limitation rules interact with another jurisdiction's substantive and limitations law.

reason: The target preserves rules of equity allowing a court to refuse relief despite the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rules of equity preserved
proposedGroups.reason: The target preserves rules of equity allowing a court to refuse relief despite the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Act does not derogate from equitable rules under which a court may refuse relief.

reason: The target contains only a repeal notation for section 27.
The target contains only a repeal notation for section 27.1.
The target contains only a repeal notation for section 27.2.
Section 28 substitutes court-proceeding language for action and cause-of-action language in Arbitration Act limitation provisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Arbitration Act limitation wording amendments
proposedGroups.reason: Section 28 substitutes court-proceeding language for action and cause-of-action language in Arbitration Act limitation provisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Arbitration Act amendments recast arbitration limitation wording around court proceedings and claims presented in arbitration.

reason: Section 29 substitutes a two-year limitation period tied to when the plaintiff knew or ought reasonably to have known of the conduct.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Business Corporations Act two-year knowledge limitation
proposedGroups.reason: Section 29 substitutes a two-year limitation period tied to when the plaintiff knew or ought reasonably to have known of the conduct.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the substituted two-year knowledge-based limitation for the Business Corporations Act provision.

reason: The target is a technical consequential amendment to the Defamation Act that repeals and updates cross-references rather than stating a standalone limitation rule.
